executive_assessment.text: Named Mapuche coastal and riverine livelihoods provide local context, alongside historical land and water disputes. Those disputes are not attributed to climate change.
Viña del Mar and Valparaíso fire findings distinguish physical losses, protection needs and response constraints; small-sample perceptions are not prevalence.
National urban/rural water-access differences and the 2026 sector plan identify service and institutional priorities. Basin pilots and training reach are outputs, not measured adaptation effects.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-04-10 reports: The study places Lafkenche communities in coastal Carahue, Puerto Saavedra, Toltén and Teodoro Schmidt; Wenteche farming communities lie along the Cautín and Quepe rivers.

Source dated 2024-04-10 reports: Participants identify community organization, territorial knowledge, medicinal plants and seed-saving as adaptation capacities; culturally appropriate rural water systems and government coordination are proposed.
Source dated 2024-03-07 reports: February 2024 fires affected six regions; Valparaíso had 14,954 ha damaged and 6,587 homes destroyed; FIBE recorded 4,163 severely affected children.
Source dated 2024-03-07 reports: UNICEF interviewed 44 people in 14 Viña del Mar locations; leading reported needs were protection, waste collection and drinking water.

UNICEF's rapid interviews after the February 2024 fires in Viña del Mar identify displacement, family separation and protection concerns. Reported perceptions of local insecurity and physical/sexual violence are not population prevalence, a measured increase caused by fire, or conflict data.
Source dated 2024-03-07 reports: Fire damage caused water cuts; emergency taps/tanks were installed, but UNICEF noted coordination problems and water shortages for cooking and washing.

Source dated 2026-09-28 reports: The plan's implementation developed 38 basin-security indicators piloted in Camiña, Maipo, Valdivia and Seno Andrew with 195 participants; a municipal water-action kit reached representatives of more than 170 municipalities.

Source dated 2025-07-03 reports: The resolution locates the historic Mapuche–State territorial conflict mainly in Biobío, La Araucanía, Los Ríos and Los Lagos and cites territorial dispossession; the commission was tasked to assess land claims and facilitate regional dialogue.

Source dated 2025-07-03 reports: The resolution says 99.59% of Indigenous land-fund purchases through 2024 occurred in the four regions and were for Mapuche applicants; 1,131 applications remained pending when recommendations were delivered.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 12 of 12 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No inspected source establishes a climate-change-to-armed/political-violence pathway in Chile; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.
The Mapuche-specific climate chain is workshop-based and conceptual; public commune-level indicators disaggregated for Indigenous communities were not found.
No inspected source showed territorial insecurity disrupting ongoing climate adaptation or routine water services; UNICEF's reported safety concerns are tied to the February 2024 wildfire emergency.
The 2024 UNFCCC BTR PDF timed out and the official repository link for the water-plan PDF returned a cache miss; the accessible DGA plan summary was used for water-plan claims.

Mapuche territorial disputes, dispossession and water-related vulnerability are documented, but their co-occurrence does not establish climate-caused political violence or insecurity interrupting adaptation.
The post-fire protection assessment is a small rapid-interview exercise. Perceived safety and violence concerns do not establish a fire-caused increase or representative prevalence.
A conceptual coastal-water projection without a stated period was excluded rather than assigning a medium-term horizon. Indigenous-disaggregated local exposure information remains incomplete.
The September 2026 water-plan account reports formal measures, pilot indicators and training, not evaluated service improvements or hydrological effects.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
